details.label: Summary
details.text: Thunderstorms will pose a risk of severe wind gusts and large hail during the next couple hours

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Several thunderstorms have recently intensified along a subtle surface boundary and in a zone of enhanced low-level convergence near a surface low in east-central CO. This activity is evolving along the eastern periphery of a large-scale ridge, where around 40 kt of effective shear is promoting convective organization (including supercells). These storms should continue tracking slowly southward along a buoyancy gradient, where a deeply mixed PBL will promote severe wind gusts over the next couple hours. Isolated instances of large hail will also be possible with the longer-lived supercell structures

details.label: Summary
details.text: An increase in thunderstorm intensity is possible during the next few hours. Damaging winds and large hail are still the main concerns, though a tornado or two cannot be ruled out

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Over the last 30 minutes or so, a couple thunderstorms have increased in intensity across northern IL and far east-central IA, as a subtle frontal wave low approaches the area from the west. In particular, one evolving supercell is interacting with a remnant outflow boundary in parts of Lee, La Salle, and Bureau Counties IL. Given an estimated south-southeastward storm motion (per nearby VWP), this storm could maintain residence time along the immediate warm side of the boundary and pose an increased risk of damaging winds, large hail, and possibly a tornado in the near term. Farther west, additional thunderstorms are intensifying in a zone of enhanced low-level convergence closer to the frontal wave low in northwest IL and far east-central IA. Warm/moist inflow for these storms and 30-40 kt of 0-6 km shear (per nearby VWP data) oriented perpendicular to the zone of low-level convergence should promote an increase in thunderstorm organization/intensity during the next few hours. Damaging winds and large hail continue to be the main concerns, though a tornado or two will also be possible, given some increase in low-level shear ahead of the frontal wave during the next few hours

details.label: Summary
details.text: Locally damaging wind may continue through the early evening

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Extensive deep convection is ongoing from southeast GA into parts of the Carolinas, which earlier produced scattered reports of wind damage through the afternoon. While storm organization has generally been limited by weak to modest deep-layer shear, a relatively vigorous line is ongoing east of Charlotte to Greensboro, NC. A narrow plume of moderate buoyancy in advance of this line will continue to support a short-term wind-damage threat. However, the longevity of the threat with this line may be limited by the relatively cooler and less unstable conditions downstream, due to earlier convection and related outflow. Otherwise, sporadic wind damage remains possible from southeast GA into eastern SC< where deep-layer shear is weak, but a corridor of warmer temperatures and steeper low-level lapse rates will remain in place through early evening, in advance of ongoing storms

details.label: Summary
details.text: The area is being monitored for an increase in severe-thunderstorm potential. The primary concerns are large hail and severe wind gusts. A watch issuance is possible

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Isolated thunderstorms are evolving along a SE/NW-oriented confluence axis extending from parts of northwest NE toward the Black Hills. This activity is potentially being aided by a subtle midlevel impulse cresting the ridge in the northern Plains. The UNR 18Z sounding sampled steep deep-layer lapse rates and a long/mostly straight hodograph (around 40 kt of effective shear) -- which will support splitting supercell structures and organized clusters. The primary concern will be large hail and robust outflow/severe wind gusts. Given the subtle large-scale forcing for ascent and some lingering low-level inhibition, storm coverage is uncertain. Convective trends will be monitored in the near term, and a watch issuance is possible
